utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you remember what sort of vehicle Dragomir Milosevic arrived in, if indeed he did arrive in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not arrive in a vehicle. It is not safe to get there in a vehicle. He arrived accompanied by the company commander, and there was no driver with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And before I go on, you mentioned the company commander, and I should have asked this earlier. Could you tell us which company your platoon was in and who this company commander was, please?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the 1st Company, and the company commander was Vukota Lekovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you recall what time of day it was that General Milosevic arrived?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon, before dark, as far as I can remember, because one could not see completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So after all these years, 12 years and a little bit, you can't remember what month this happened, you can remember that it happened in the afternoon, you cannot remember the names of any of the members of the general's entourage. Is it safe to say, Mr. Elez, that the only significant thing you can remember about this occasion is General Milosevic's saying to you not to shoot civilians? Is that -- is that the only thing that stands out in your mind after 12 years?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that because, as I said, it was not dark yet, but Milosevic could not be seen properly. When coming to combat positions, he informs the company commander and he toured with him, at least --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, but he said what he repeated just now. He remembered who was with him, whereas the Prosecutor is suggesting that he did not know who he had come from, but he already said that he was with the company commander. He said the name and the surname. The first name was Vukota, and I cannot remember the last name now, so he said the name and surname of the person he had come with. He remembered that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What was put to him was whether it was safe to say that the only significant thing that he could remember was the general saying not shoot civilians, and whether that was the only thing that stood out in his mind after 12 years. And he's seeking to answer that. And I don't understand your point. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, but before that, he said that he did not remember anything but that, whereas the witness did say that he did remember who he had come with. In response to a series of questions he said that he remembered that he had come with the company commander. However, what was suggested to him was that the only thing he remembered was this conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, it's being said that you misrepresented the evidence in suggesting that that was the only thing the witness recollected, that he did recollect other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Elez, you testified that this was the only time during your service with the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps that the commander of your corps came to visit your unit. It was the only time he came to visit; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's why I remember, because it was the only time. I remember there were other conversations but I cannot remember all of that, and I couldn't see him properly because he came in order to seek shelter into the premises and it was dark and that is why I remember things the way I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So there were, as you just said, other conversations but you don't remember those other conversations; is that what you just testified to?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were other soldiers there that he talked to and they were talking. I remember what I said. Perhaps there was more informal talk, like, "How are you guys? How are your families? Are you hungry? What are your uniforms like? Do you have enough ammunition?" I can't remember exactly. It's hard to remember all of that but you can remember some of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes. I know it's hard to remember those things. I know that this was 12 years ago. But what I'm putting to you, sir, that a visit by such a high-ranking officer, the only time that this occurred during the war, must have been a pretty memorable experience for you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you consider memorable, because at that time we talked a lot amongst us. We had heard a lot of stories, and the topic was the suffering of civilians and that's what we talked about too.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: It really doesn't matter, Mr. Elez, what I consider memorable. I asked if you found it memorable, the visit of -- the one-time-in-the-war visit of a senior military officer like General Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. That was memorable.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And at that time in the war, there were a lot of things that were on your mind in that trench along the Miljacka river, things like food and ammunition supply, correct?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not our job to think about either food or supplies of ammunition. When we were in our positions we didn't think about food. We tried to save our ammunition. We didn't have much in stock. I suppose there was somebody who was in charge of that, whose job it was to think about ammunition. And we had to do with the food we got.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But here is a general officer, whom you can ask about the things that are on your mind. I mean, this is, as you've described it, for a military context, a fairly informal conversation, correct?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were also other officers touring positions, like the one in charge of morale. They asked us what kind of uniforms we had. There were lots of questions on both sides. We were missing a lot of things. But we had to do with what we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: But the thing that you remember about your conversation with General Milosevic, the thing that you want to give evidence about at this Tribunal, is General Milosevic telling you not to shoot civilians? There might have been conversation about other things, like uniforms and families, but you don't remember that. What you remember is not to shoot civilians? And after all these years, that's what you remember and that's what you want to give evidence of, correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that the witness can be confronted with what he really said, but we should find the relevant passage in the transcript and confront him. Yesterday, he said something that the Prosecutor is now quoting back at him but we don't know whether he said it exactly in that way so we should find the passage in the transcript and find his own exact words that he uttered in the examination-in-chief. We need a reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is your point that the witness did say in evidence earlier that he remembered other things apart from the general telling them not to shoot civilians? Are you saying that he has testified to other things being said or to his recollection of other things? If that is so, Mr. Docherty, are you in a position to cite the passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I will be in just a moment, Your Honour. I'm just scrolling back. Your Honour, the witness said at page 49, lines 12 through -- 12 and 13, "That's why I remember because it was the only time. I remember there were other conversations but I cannot remember all of that and I couldn't see him properly." So I take that, Your Honour, as the witness saying that there were other conversations but he doesn't remember them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, are you able to draw our attention to any passage in which the witness said he recollected the general saying other things to them?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I supplement my last answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Above that at page 49, lines 20 through 25, the end of the page, "There were other soldiers there that he talked to and they were talking. I remember what I said. Perhaps there was more informal talk, like 'How are you guys? How are your families? Are you hungry? What are your uniforms like, do you have enough ammunition?" I can't remember exactly. It's hard to remember all of that, but you can remember some of it." So again, Your Honour, I take that at least as the witness saying, yes, there was other conversation but all I remember is the injunction against shooting civilians, all that I remember with precision. And I focus on the word "perhaps."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 12th page, 14th line. That's the passage which shows the subject discussed. And there is a whole paragraph in line 12 which shows --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Give us the citation, please, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since I can't speak English, I would like to ask my colleague to read this.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISAILOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, page 12, Mr. Tapuskovic asked a question, so I'm talking about line 12. [In English] "But tell me, did you have a" -- [Interpretation] So for me I would have interpreted that as, "Have you ever met General Dragomir Milosevic?" And then after that, the witness answered, between lines 14 and page 13, line 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, I believe it is slightly inaccurate to put this suggestion that you have been putting to the witness because there is in the passage cited other things mentioned by the witness in relation to the general's visit. You were putting to him that, is the general's remark about civilians the only thing that he remembers from his visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think -- I think that this point has been beaten half to death. What I am attempting to put to the witness, and I'll move on now, is that the witness remembers with clarity, with precision, this injunction against shooting civilians and that as to everything else, despite how memorable the occasion was and how unusual the occasion was, the witness remembers with clarity one point that is helpful to the Defence. That is what I am putting. That is what I would argue from all of the evidence and as I say, the evidence will be what it will be. The record is as it is. And I think that both sides can argue such inferences as are there to be made. I don't think I'm being told that I misrepresented the record. I certainly did not mean to do so. But as I say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At this stage, I'm going to end it. At this stage I'm going to end this long debate. I'm not going to allow the question to be put to the witness. It appears to me to be more appropriate for submission in closing arguments. We have the transcript. We have the witness's evidence. And we'll have to make up our minds about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could we please see Defence Exhibit 219?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you see that in front of you, Mr. Elez?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And in the upper left-hand corner, there is a date on this document, isn't there, of 11th of July 1995? Do you see that and have I read it out correctly?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I want to direct your attention to paragraph number 3, "Targets for attack." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm going to read these to you, artillery positions, that is a military target, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Tanks are a military target, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: There are the initials at least on the English side, "PAT." That's an anti-aircraft gun, isn't it, and that is a military target, correct?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: "Stores of weapon load," military target, Mr. Elez?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I don't know what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sorry. But just one more question. We are past time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm actually -- could we take it now? I'm about to get into something more contentious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Ready to proceed, Mr. Elez?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Elez, Exhibit 219, Defence Exhibit 219 is still on the screen in front of you. I'm really following up on a question that Judge Harhoff asked earlier. Communication facilities, armies have communication facilities, don't they?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: They have things like field telephones and radio nets and other means of communicating; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Bridges, armies have bridges, don't they, sir?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not armies that have bridges. Settlements, population centres, have bridges.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And during wartime, armies use those bridges, don't they?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And knocking down a bridge can be a great detriment to an enemy army, can't it, by making it difficult for that army to move around, can't it?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If we could move on, please, to Defence Exhibit 217, please? This is a document that Mr. Tapuskovic had some questions for you on your direct examination. Do you remember the document, Mr. Elez?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: What's the date of this document, Mr. Elez?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1st July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity, Mr. Elez, to look at the amended indictment in this case?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What amended indictment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Let me take it in stages. You understand that the charges in this case are contained in a legal document called an indictment? Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to read that indictment before coming to the Netherlands to give testimony in this case or have you had a chance to look at it since arriving in the Netherlands a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have occasion to see the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If you have not read the indictment, are you aware from any other source that the last scheduled sniping incident alleged in that indictment has a date of 3rd of May of 1995?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Then let's go back to the document. And I'm going to ask you to look at some of the positions that it indicates the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina has attacked. And then we are going to look at a photograph and I'm going to ask you to point these places out on a photograph. There is a reference to the butcher's. Do you see that? I'm sorry, Mr. Elez, did you hear me my -- oh, you're waiting for the translation, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any photograph, I don't have any image.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Oh, not yet. I'm sorry, I wasn't clear. I'm going to ask you about some things that are mentioned in this document, and after that we are going to look at a photograph. I apologise for the misunderstanding. Do you see there a reference to a butcher's in the document?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Direct him to the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could you look at the paragraph that begins, "On 26 June 1995, the 4/115 Brigade POS" and then a little further on there are three locations specified. Is one of them the butcher's?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see it now. I hadn't read everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And do you know the butcher's that this is referring to?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: There is also a reference, same sentence, to the Investbank building, isn't there?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And as someone who has lived in Grbavica, would you be able to show us the Investbank building on a photograph?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And then the last specific place that is mentioned is the red building. Would you be able, if you were shown a photograph, to show us the red building?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And then there is actually one more place, which is this document talks about a raid in which four -- excuse me, three four-storey houses were seized; is that correct? It's in the sentence that begins, "The capture of this aggressor feature." And then there is a parentheses and in there the aggressor feature is described as a group of three four-storey buildings. Do you see where I'm reading that?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And now let's look at the photograph, and if we could please see 65 ter number 02825? Mr. Elez, do you see a photograph on the monitor in front of you, an aerial shot? At the moment, sir, I'm just asking if the photograph has appeared on your monitor.

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There is an image but that's not the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: On this image, do you see any of the buildings that you -- that we were talking about a minute ago? Do you see, for example, the Invest building?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: How am I supposed to point it out? I can see it. I can see Investbank.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And now I'm going to ask you, with the help of the usher, to put a B on the Investbank building, B, the English word "bank."

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you see the red building? And if so, please mark it R.

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you -- is the butcher's shop -- I'm sorry. Did you mean to say something? I'll stop.

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do actually. There is another one next to the one I marked and that one is also red, but I believe "the" red building is the one I marked, although there are two red ones on the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you for that. The red building referred to in the combat report we were just reading is the one you've marked, in your opinion, correct?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And then lastly, if it's on the photograph, can you mark the butcher's shop with the word -- with the letter S?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: There used to be two butcher's shops here before. I know the city well. Can I show you?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Would you, please?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll put a dot on it. In this housing complex, there is one butcher's shop and there is one on the corner. [Marks]. I marked the roof. Here on top -- sorry, on the corner there is one butcher shop. I don't know which one you meant in your question but I believe it was the one on the corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That's fine. There are two butcher's shops and they are in roughly the same area, is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Why don't you just mark -- I apologise. I didn't mean to speak over you. Could you just mark an S on both of them, so there will be two Ss and that's for "shop."

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, could this photograph as marked please be admitted into evidence but remain on the screen? I have a couple of questions about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P764, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Elez, we were talking just a couple of minutes ago about the date of that combat report which you said was the 1st of July of 1995. And is it correct that that combat report refers to attacks on what they call aggressor positions at the locations you have marked on Prosecution Exhibit 764?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Doesn't that mean, Mr. Elez, that as of the date right before that combat report, these positions were under the control of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, there was also a reference in that report to a number of four-storey -- or three-storey houses or buildings, excuse me, being seized. From the -- was there enough information in that combat report for you to tell where those buildings were?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which buildings were meant because there are quite a few of them here. Which four-storey buildings did they mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If you don't know, that's fine and that's understandable, and we'll move on. Now, right in front of the building that you have marked B, runs the Miljacka river; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And so on the bottom portion of Prosecution Exhibit 764, from the Miljacka down to the bottom of the photograph, we are looking at territory under the command or the control of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: From the building marked B, the Investbank building, someone on the upper floors could fire into the area at the bottom of the photograph, the Sarajevo neighbourhood of Marin Dvor; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside the Investbank building, there were no positions on top floors. There was a position on the first floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Sir, excuse me, I have to stop you.

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I finish?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you, sir. I asked you if a person in the Investbank building could fire into Marin Dvor from that building. With all respect, I did not ask you what positions the SRK had in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you have any particular section of Marin Dvor in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I do, and I'll get to that in a question or two. I wanted to get to the general point first.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Elez, I'll just ask the question again. From the building marked B, you can fire into Marin Dvor, can't you?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: On the left-hand margin of Prosecution Exhibit 764, do you see a street running north and south?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: From your experience as an infantryman, you know, don't you, that firing down a natural funnel like that is an aid to accurate infantry fire, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And the building marked B sits at the end, the northern end, of such a funnel, does it not?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand which building you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you see on Prosecution Exhibit 764 a building which you have marked with the letter B?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That building sits at the top, the northern end, of a funnel for infantry fire formed by that street that runs north-south along the left-hand margin of this photograph, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The witness has answered yes, but I don't see that building as being at the end. If the funnel is formed by the street, then the building B is not at the top of it. That would be the Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm sorry, the Metalka building, there are two north-south streets here. There's the one in the centre of the photograph and that does terminate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: -- in the Metalka building, but there is another street on the far left margin. It's -- in fact, the left-hand curve, I think, is out of the picture, it's so close to the edge. That's the one I was referring to. And with that, Mr. President, I have no further questions. That concludes my cross-examination. Thank you, Mr. Elez, and a safe trip home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But I still don't understand the question because the evidence, the preponderance of evidence, has related to the other street.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Not to the one that you have mentioned there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And that's why I was misled.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I try not to mislead judges but -- no. I was simply pointing out that this building also shoots down a natural funnel into the Marin Dvor area, but I concur with you that most of the evidence has concerned shooting from the Metalka building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I don't have too many things.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since we have this photograph in front of us, you already spoke about this document and you mentioned Miska Jovanovica and Zagrebacka streets. Were these actions aimed at Miska Jovanovica and Zagrebacka streets? By looking at this photograph can you show whether one can see at least approximately parts of either of the streets?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: One can see on this photograph a part of Zagrebacka street. This is this part next to Investbank marked B and part of Beogradska street, a small portion in front of the red building marked R.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please show the Judges where this street is and put a line along the -- this street that is in the photograph, Miska Jovanovica or Zagrebacka street?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zagrebacka street is here. It extends further on towards Grbavica. Beogradska street is this little portion that you can see here and it goes further inwards. Miska Jovanovica street cannot be seen or Ljubljanska street or rather part of the upper section of Ljubljanska street can be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And where is Zagrebacka street?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zagrebacka street is what I marked here going by Investbanka, inwards, and part of it can also be seen here, going to the inner section of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, looking at this street as a whole, are there any four-storey buildings on this street or on this other street if one was -- were able to see it?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what four-storey buildings are in question here. I cannot establish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You don't know in this photograph. How long are these streets?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Viewing from the Vrbanja bridge towards Vrace and it goes from Skenderija, so there is a view from Skenderija as well across Vrbanja on the other bank of the Miljacka, all the way to the Vrace junction and further on, the length is about 700, 800 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you spoke about the 26th of June 1995, you said, and you drew and marked these buildings, can you tell me now what you first marked with an R, in which part of the building was this woman killed, the one that you mentioned, a Serbian woman, as you said, if you can mark it?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the mother of one of our fighters. I said his name. And she was living in the frontal part of the building, and I'll mark it with a dot. [Marks]. I cannot be specific about the flat in which she lived. I know that this part was seized by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I think that is in the front. And this part was seized. I don't know how long they stayed inside. They used to come in, burst into it, come again during the night. So it wasn't safe to keep this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you put a letter M?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, all this surrounding this and other buildings, it says here how many shells landed here. What are these buildings around, regardless of in whose territory they were? Who was living there? Was there the army? Who lived in those buildings?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are all residential buildings. People lived there, tenants, former tenants who had been living there before the conflict broke out. The army took up positions on the edges of these residential buildings because this is urban warfare. You cannot move away the battlefield to a field and build trenches and that is how they established a line. Partly they managed to defend themselves, partly they didn't. For instance, this building was captured and it remained like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you spoke about the 26th, you now said, mentioned a series of buildings, the butcher shop, the red building, et cetera. My learned friend, the Prosecutor, asked you about the document which says that the capture of the aggressor's feature made up of three four-storey buildings, what does this mean? Who captured these four-storey buildings which you don't see here, as you said yourself?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which four-storey buildings this referred to, I cannot say. But it was captured by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this photograph, as it is, be given number -- a number as a Defence Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it may be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D220, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just look at Defence Exhibit 215? It's the map with Mojmilo marked on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In response to the Prosecutor's question you said that you had made a mistake. However, what I would like to ask you is the following: This road that passes here, with respect to Mojmilo, in geographical terms, where was this road with regard to Mojmilo hill, geographically speaking?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: This road, Vrace-Lukavica, is at the foot hill with regard to Mojmilo hill, from which there was constant enemy fire coming. It was impossible to use that road. It was risky. That involved the Lukavica neighbourhood, the neighbourhood of Dobrinja, and as I said, there was fire coming from Mojmilo to Grbavica and also on the other side at Lukavica and Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Elez, is that the road that made you relinquish your duty as the platoon commander partly or was the whole road the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: Vaso Elez [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not that road. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: That is why I asked you. I wasn't quite sure. Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Elez, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next witness, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the next witness is a protected one, P53 -- sorry, T53. He has the measures of pseudonym and image distortion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please sit. And you may begin, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I would first like to show the witness the paper with his personal details, to get that out of the way. That would be our first Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be admitted as D221 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As you know, I appear here as Defence counsel for General Dragomir Milosevic, and I will try to go over a few matters with you very quickly, to cover your background first of all. Could you please speak at a moderate rate and look at the transcript and follow the cursor and do not start answering before the cursor stops. You were born on (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T53
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, this was supposed to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell me if you have any military training or, rather, did you have any military training at the moment the conflict broke out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T53
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, apart from the training I received during my compulsory military service, I have no other training or skills.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have anything to do with the Yugoslav People's Army apart from serving in 1984?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T53
utterances.text: After my regular military service, I was occasionally engaged in the reserve force, but that happened once a year or once in two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since I have not a lot of time for you, I'll try to cover a couple of questions quickly. How long did you continue in your job at the factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T53
utterances.text: My last day there, which was a Monday, I believe, the 6th of April 1992, I asked the deputy manager to grant me my annual leave in the duration of 15 days, hoping that in the meantime things would calm down and that I will be able to go to work as usual, because at that point it was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you what prompted you to ask that 15-day leave? Did anything happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T53
utterances.text: Well, fighting had already started. Shooting began from directions that I was unable to determine, and because I felt unsafe using my car, I wanted to take a break and see how the situation would develop from then on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I think you misunderstood my warning about the cursor. You don't have to make pauses during your answer. Please continue. Is there anything else you wanted to add?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T53
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What happened next? Were there any new developments that took you by surprise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T53
utterances.text: I was taken by surprise by the combat activities in my immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain that a bit? Did you see anything from your vantage point? Where was your home at the time? And what could be observed from your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS T53
utterances.text: My home was in the (redacted). If you have a map I could show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I want to cover this quickly. Just tell us where it is. But first we have to go into private session. And this bit would have to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 11th day of June, 2007, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
